workPackageTitle: Pure NUnit test projects and Godot integration-test harness
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91 § Verification registry).
The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002. Until it lands, the shape here matches tests/verification/FND-001.json exactly.

The pure tiers (MechaMiner.Simulation.Tests, MechaMiner.Content.Tests, MechaMiner.Persistence.Tests) never launch Godot. The engine tier (MechaMiner.Game.Tests) launches the pinned Godot executable as an external process and asserts the emitted report; it holds no Godot type, so game/ remains the only Godot-referencing project (docs/technical/115 § Accepted project boundary).

VER-FND-003-007 through VER-FND-003-010 deliberately assert the runner report rather than the Godot process exit code. A headless Godot launch exits 0 even when the C# script on the boot node fails to load, so exit status alone is not a gate; FND-001 hit this empirically and recorded it in tests/verification/FND-001.json.

The sample tests prove the harness pattern, not domain behavior: at FND-003 the pure production projects contain no domain code. Every later stream replaces these samples with real subject tests using the same shared support types.

Status is current status: an entry whose implementing task has not landed yet is 'registered'. TASK-FND-003-001 entries are implemented in this revision; TASK-FND-003-002 entries flip to 'implemented' when the Godot integration runner lands. Both sets of entries were written before either implementation.

entries.summary: All three pure test projects discover and execute a nonzero number of NUnit tests through the standard test-fast verb without launching Godot.
Every randomized test logs its seed and version identity before the randomized body executes, so an aborted or hanging run still names its seed.
A randomized failure prints a one-command reproduction description and preserves the minimized failing input as a file beneath artifacts/.

Floating-point comparison in the shared harness is only reachable through an explicitly named tolerance; no unnamed approximate-equality helper exists, and a tolerance constructed without a name or with a nonpositive magnitude is rejected.

Golden comparison uses canonical ordered reviewable text, reports a reviewable line diff on mismatch, and an update run rewrites the golden but still fails so a golden can never be accepted merely to make a run green.
A property test compares an optimized implementation against a deliberately simple reference model over generated inputs, within a named tolerance where the comparison is not exact.
The Godot integration runner executes a passing case headlessly and the host test accepts it only from the emitted report, which carries the engine version, renderer, case ID, and assertion list.
A deliberately failing engine case is reported as failed with its failing assertion, and the host test fails, proving the runner cannot pass a broken case.
A hanging engine case is terminated at its bounded timeout, produces no report, and is classified as timed out rather than passed, because a headless Godot process can exit 0 or never exit at all.
An engine case that declares an artifact writes it beneath artifacts/ and references it from its report, and the host test asserts both the reference and the file.

test-fast runs the pure tiers and the build-policy fixtures only, and launches no Godot process at all, observed with a tripwire: an executable named godot is placed first on PATH and in MECHAMINER_GODOT for every pure test process, and the tier fails if it was ever invoked. A negative control proves the assertion can fail. The tripwire's coverage is the pure NUnit test processes and nothing else, which this entry and the assertion itself both used to overstate. VerbContext.RunRepositoryScript passes no environment, so the gate scripts test-fast runs are started with the verb host's own PATH and never see the shim; their nested ./build.sh invocations do launch the pinned engine - build/verify-verbs.sh probes it through doctor - and an empty sentinel says nothing about them. Observed: with verify-verbs.sh wired into test-fast, real doctor calls launched Godot and this assertion still reported that it was never invoked. The recorded assertion now says only what the shim can see. FOLLOW-UP (FND-003, which owns this code): propagate the tripwire environment through RunRepositoryScript. The hard part is not the plumbing - a gate script legitimately runs ./build.sh doctor and doctor's job is to probe the pinned engine, so arming the shim for gate scripts either fails doctor or needs an exception for it, and an exception is how a tripwire stops being one. That question has to be answered before the plumbing.
test-main runs the pure tiers plus the Godot engine tier after a headless import, and returns the owning tier's exit class rather than success after partial work.
